To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transaminase and the dehydrogenases involved in leucine degradation are present in the soluble and mitochondrial fractions of muscle, respectively.
leucine, valine and isoleucine are oxidized in muscle via transamination to 4-methyloxo acid and oxidative decarboxylations to acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA.

Leucine is transaminated to the 2-oxo acid, which is then decarboxylized by a mitochondrial dehydrogenase, and that the transaminase is regulated by Ca2+ concentration, whereas the dehydrogenation is regulated by ATP concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of branched-chain amino acid metabolism in skeletal muscle.
the elucidation of the metabolic pathways and regulation of the branched chain amino acids, leucine, valine and isoleucine in skeletal muscle.
the regulation of the metabolism of the branched chain amino acids in muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transamination of leucine is the rate-limiting reaction for the degradation of leucine.
the pathway of leucine degradation in skeletal muscle consists of transamination of leucine to 4-metyl-2-oxovalerate followed by oxidative decarboxylate of the latter compound.
the pathway of leucine degradation is transamination to 4-methylene-2-oxovalerate and oxidative decarboxlation to 2-oxoisovalerate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in rat skeletal muscle the transamination of leucine is the rate-limiting reaction in the oxidation of this amino acid, and that the transaminase reaction is regulated by intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
the pathway for leucine degradation in muscle is similar to the pathway in other mammalian tissues.
the pathway of leucine metabolism in rat muscle is: leucine + 2-oxo-glutarate = 4-methylpentanoate + glutamate; 4-methyl 2-oxopentaonate + CoA + NAD+ + TPP = 2-methylbutyryl-CoA + NADH + CO2 + H+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the branched-chain amino acid transaminase (BCAT) and branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) activities in skeletal muscle are tightly regulated.
the branched-chain amino acids (BCAA) leucine, valine and isoleucine are metabolized in the muscle, liver and kidneys.
leucine is transaminated to a-ketoisocaproate (Ki), which is then oxidatively decarbonylated to form acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate.
